meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: خضرا, plural: خضر).

examples.trans: Pass beside the green pharmacy.
Put the green herbs on the eggs.

meanings.note: Polite Jordanian title for any man ('sir / Mr') as well as 'teacher' or 'professor'.

examples.trans: Please have a seat, sir.
Good morning, gentlemen.

meanings.note: Feminine noun; the plural أغاني (aghaani) is the one you hear most.

examples.trans: This is an old song my grandmother loves.
We listen to songs in the car every morning.

meanings.note: Name of the month of May in the Levantine calendar.

examples.trans: My birthday is in May.
In May the weather gets nice in Amman.

meanings.note: Parts of the body in pairs are feminine in Arabic; 'my hands' is إيديي (iideyyi).

examples.trans: He washed his hands with warm water.
I planted the flowers with my own hand.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتصل, بيتصل).

examples.trans: Call the lost-and-found office right away.
You called us on Tuesday.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The reception desk is beside the door.
Thank you for the warm welcome.

meanings.note: Command to a male to wait.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, I have an idea!
The suitcase is still waiting for its owner.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The guest arrived Wednesday night.
We meet on Wednesday morning.

meanings.note: The holy day in Islam and the weekend in Jordan.

examples.trans: The family gathers every Friday at noon.
On Friday the street is quiet.

meanings.note: The day of the week, Saturday.

examples.text: كل سبت الصبح بنمشي عسوق الحارة.
examples.trans: Every Saturday morning we walk to the neighbourhood market.

examples.text: الخبز الطازة بيجهز يوم السبت الساعة تمانية.
examples.trans: Fresh bread is ready on Saturday at eight o'clock.

meanings.note: Used directly before nouns or pronouns (بدل ستة 'instead of six') and before ما + verb (بدل ما تستنى 'instead of waiting').

examples.text: اشرب شاي سخن بالنعنع بدل القهوة بالليل.
examples.trans: Drink hot mint tea instead of coffee at night.

examples.text: ضل معنا تلات أيام بس بدل أسبوع كامل.
examples.trans: We only have three days left instead of a whole week.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: بلديات.

examples.trans: He works in the contracts office at the municipality.
The municipal building is next to the square.

meanings.note: The musical instrument.

examples.trans: The sound of the piano is warm and calm.
I learned piano when I was young.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: تانية, plural: تانيين).

examples.trans: Room four is on the second floor.
There is a second sheet behind the letter.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Heritage law protects old houses.
Amman has beautiful architectural heritage.

meanings.note: The number 9.

examples.trans: The quietness in the courtyard is nine out of ten!
She came back in just nine minutes!

meanings.note: Verbal noun of فتّش ('to inspect, check officially').

examples.text: لجنة التفتيش من البلدية جاية يوم الأربعا.
examples.trans: The inspection team from City Hall is coming on Wednesday.
The whole kitchen is clean and ready for inspection.

meanings.note: The standalone form of the number 3.

examples.trans: Three years was a long time.
One, two, three!

meanings.note: The number 30.

examples.trans: They have given us thirty days in the letter.
The bill is thirty-eight dinars.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: تليفونات.

examples.trans: The phone rang on the reception desk.
I wrote the phone number in the notebook.

meanings.note: A unit of time or the feminine ordinal for second.

examples.trans: Wait one second, please.
He came back ten seconds later on the dot.

meanings.note: The standard Levantine Arabic word for 'inside' or 'inwards'.

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
The water is flowing inside!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: حروف.

examples.trans: Two small letters are written on the corner.
The letters of her name are clear on the zip.

meanings.note: Can mean a physical line, a phone line, a bus route, or handwriting.

examples.trans: Your handwriting on the card is clear and neat.
Stay with me on the line a second.

meanings.note: Very frequent Jordanian verb: خليني ('let me'), خلينا ('let us'), خليك ('stay!'), خلي ('keep/leave').

examples.trans: Let us open the door together.
Hot bread makes people pleasant!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بخبز, بيخبز).

examples.text: اخبزي قطع زوايا كتير يا سلمى!
examples.trans: Bake plenty of corner pieces, Salma!

examples.text: قديش بيقدر فرنك يخبز كل صبح؟
examples.trans: How much can your oven bake every morning?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: دوائر.

examples.trans: A paper arrived from the property department.
The department office is downtown.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian verb meaning 'to manage, run (a shop/inn)' and in دير بالك ('take care!').

examples.text: عمتي كانت تدير قاعة الشاي لحالها.
examples.trans: My aunt used to run the tea room on her own.

examples.text: مازن بيدير النزل مع طارق ونور وسلمى.
examples.trans: Mazen runs the inn with Tariq, Nour, and Salma.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: دفاتر.

examples.trans: We wrote the name in the booking ledger.
I forgot my leather notebook on the table.

meanings.note: One of the four seasons: صيف summer, خريف autumn, شتا winter, ربيع spring.

examples.trans: Spring in Amman is short and lovely.
In spring we go out to the hills.

meanings.note: Used constantly in the respectful phrase الله يرحمه / الله يرحمها ('may God rest his/her soul; the late...').

examples.text: جدي الله يرحمه هو اللي زرع شجرة الياسمين.
examples.trans: My late grandfather is the one who planted the jasmine tree.

examples.text: عمتي الله يرحمها كانت تحب الموسيقى كتير.
examples.trans: My late aunt used to love music dearly.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: رسايل.

examples.trans: An official letter arrived at noon.
We read the letter line by line.

meanings.note: Verbal noun of زار ('to visit').

examples.trans: Your brother's visit made us very happy today.
They moved the date of the visit forward to Wednesday.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ساحات.

examples.trans: The courtyard has a big jasmine tree.
We sat drinking tea in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday word for an hour of time, a wristwatch, or a wall clock.

examples.trans: What time is it right now, please?
We arrived an hour ago on the dot.

meanings.note: The number 6.

examples.trans: Room six is on the second floor.
I have six lemons in the basket.

meanings.note: Core word in مع السلامة! ('goodbye!', literally 'with safety') and الحمد لله عالسلامة ('glad you arrived safely').

examples.trans: Goodbye, see you tomorrow!
Thank goodness for your safe arrival.

meanings.note: Everyday word for a year.

examples.trans: The building is eighty years old.
I have not seen him for three years.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: A staple beverage in Jordanian culture, typically served with mint or sage.

examples.trans: Please have a glass of hot mint tea.
There is black tea and coffee at breakfast.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بشغل, بيشغل).

examples.trans: Can we turn the water heater on now?
She started up the coffee machine in the morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian interrogative pronoun for 'what'.

examples.trans: What is that sound?
What is written on the sheet, Rami?

meanings.note: Everyday spoken Jordanian noun for 'the morning' (الصبح in the morning, كل صبح every morning).

examples.trans: I drink black coffee every morning.
The morning bread is still hot.

meanings.note: Adjective used for size (small) or age (young), masculine singular.

examples.trans: We found a little wooden train in the bag.
There are two small streets on the left.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: صفحات.

examples.trans: Read the second page of the letter.
The notebook fell open to the middle page.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: صناديق.

examples.trans: The screwdriver is inside the toolbox.
We moved four boxes out of the hallway.

meanings.note: Nisba adjective from صوت ('voice, sound'); رسالة صوتية means 'voice message'.

examples.trans: I left you a short voice message on the phone.
The acoustic insulation in the sunroom is excellent.

meanings.note: Very common Levantine verb meaning to stay, remain, or keep doing something.

examples.trans: Family is what remains.
My teacup stayed intact inside the suitcase!

ضوّى.gloss: to light up; shine; switch on a light

meanings.en: to light up; shine; switch on a light
meanings.note: Used for a lamp that glows and for the person who switches it on (ضوي الضو 'turn on the light').

examples.trans: The new lamp gives good light.
Turn the light on, the room is dark.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun (feminine: ضيفة). Plural: ضيوف.

examples.trans: The guests are coming down to breakfast now.
We welcomed every guest with a smile.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعرف, بيعرف).

examples.trans: I recognized your neat handwriting in two seconds!
Do you know anyone here in Amman?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: علالي.

examples.trans: The attic room on the third floor is sunny.
We brought the boxes down from the attic.

meanings.note: Levantine progressive marker placed before a present-tense verb to show action happening right now.

examples.trans: The water is flowing inside the pipe right now!

examples.text: كنت عم بدور على دفتري هلا.
examples.trans: I was just looking for my notebook.

meanings.note: Arabic distinguishes father's sister (عمة, feminine of عمّ) from mother's sister (خالة).

examples.text: عمتي كانت تعزف عالبيانو كل يوم جمعة.
examples.trans: My paternal aunt used to play the piano every Friday.

examples.text: هاد الدفتر الأخضر هدية من عمتي.
examples.trans: This green notebook is a gift from my aunt.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعزف, بيعزف).

examples.trans: I am still waiting for you to play the scale!

examples.text: الكبير كان يعزف بيانو كل جمعة.
examples.trans: The older boy used to play piano every Friday.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for a room in a house or building.

examples.trans: We have eight comfortable rooms at the guesthouse.
Room four is ready and clean.

meanings.note: Musical loanword (from French valse) for a triple-time piano or orchestral waltz.

examples.text: عزفت سعاد فالس هادي بغرفة القزاز.
examples.trans: Suad played a gentle waltz in the sunroom.

examples.text: عنوان الورقة القديمة هو فالس الساحة.
examples.trans: The title on the old sheet is Courtyard Waltz.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: قاعات.

examples.trans: The old hall has clear acoustics.
They met in the meeting hall in the morning.

meanings.note: Preposition and adverb for time or sequence meaning 'prior to' or 'before'.

examples.text: علمت بيانو هون قبل خمسة وعشرين سنة.
examples.trans: I taught piano here twenty-five years ago.
Drink your coffee before the rush.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: قديمة, plural: قدام).

examples.trans: The courtyard has an old jasmine tree.
The old hardware shop is past the bridge.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقدم, بيقدم).

examples.trans: We serve fresh breakfast every morning.
She served the guests mint tea.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: كافيهات.

examples.trans: We opened a small café in the house courtyard.
The morning café serves all the neighbours.

meanings.note: Past tense of 'to be' for 3rd person masculine singular. Widely used as an auxiliary verb.

examples.trans: How was the bus ride?

examples.text: تاني يوم ما رح يكون ممل!
examples.trans: The second day will not be boring!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: كبيرة, plural: كبار).

examples.trans: We use this big paper ledger.
You know older brothers well!

meanings.note: Depending on vowels, it means 'he wrote' (katab) or plural 'books' (kutub).

examples.text: رح يكتب تقييم حلو عن النزل.
examples.trans: He will write a lovely review of the guesthouse.
I wrote my name and number on the card.

meanings.note: Refers generally to cake as a type of food.

examples.trans: I made chocolate cake for the kids.
Would you like a piece of cake with your tea?

meanings.note: Very common Jordanian word to indicate that an action is ongoing or hasn't happened yet.

examples.trans: Is your cup still intact?
Nobody has written anything yet.

meanings.note: The standard colloquial interrogative for 'why' in Jordanian Arabic.

examples.trans: Why did the person run off without his bag?
Why do you keep looking at the clock?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ليالي.

examples.trans: The guest arrived last night.
The neighbourhood is very quiet at night.

meanings.note: Passive participle of خبّى, to hide (something). Also heard as مخبّي.

examples.trans: The key is hidden under the rug.
We found a letter hidden in the book.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مدورة, plural: مدورين).

examples.trans: Where should I hang the round mirror?
We put a round wooden table in the corner.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form مسا (masa) alongside standard مساء in مساء الخير ('good evening').

examples.trans: The eight o'clock evening bus is arriving.
The air is calm and pleasant this evening.

meanings.note: Passive participle of سجّل ('to record, register').

examples.trans: We found a recorded message on the desk phone.
Every reservation is recorded in the front-desk ledger.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'with'; takes pronoun suffixes to express 'have on one's person' (معي 'I have with me', معك حق 'you are right').

examples.trans: You are right, Nour!
Goodbye! (lit. go with safety)

meanings.note: Often used as a noun meaning 'letter' (mail) or 'destiny' in traditional contexts.

examples.trans: What is written in the letter, Nour?
Our two names are still written in pencil.

meanings.note: One of the most basic Arabic prepositions indicating origin.

examples.trans: I am Salma from the kitchen.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Interrogative pronoun used for people.

examples.trans: Who left this envelope here?
Whose is this brown leather notebook?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنزل, بينزل).

examples.trans: Let us bring the suitcase down into the light.
Let me lower my glasses from my forehead!

meanings.note: Extremely common word used in time (e.g., 3 and a half) and measurements.

examples.trans: Breakfast starts at seven thirty.

examples.text: بس نص كاسة عصير لو سمحت.
examples.trans: Just half a glass of juice, please.

meanings.note: Singular نظارة means one pair of glasses in Arabic (نظارتي my glasses); dual نظارتين means two pairs of glasses!

examples.trans: I cannot find my glasses on the desk!
He pulled his glasses down off his forehead and laughed.

نوتة.gloss: sheet music; musical score; pocket notepad

meanings.en: sheet music; musical score; pocket notepad
meanings.note: Used across the Levant for printed or handwritten musical notation (نوتة موسيقية).

examples.text: فتحت سعاد نوتة البيانو القديمة عالصفحة الأولى.
examples.trans: Suad opened the old piano score to page one.

examples.text: كتب المؤلف النوتة بحبر أسود واضح.
examples.trans: The composer wrote the score in clear black ink.

meanings.note: Everyday demonstrative pronoun for masculine singular objects.

examples.trans: Here we use this big ledger.
This suitcase is very heavy today.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian distal demonstrative ('that over there / that past...'); feminine هديك (hadiik), plural هدولاك.

examples.text: بتذكر هداك الربيع لما فتحنا النزل؟
examples.trans: Do you remember that spring when we opened the inn?

examples.text: حط الصندوق على هداك الرف العالي.
examples.trans: Put the box on that high shelf.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بوقف, بيوقف).

examples.text: وقفوا كل شي، قديش الساعة هلا؟
examples.trans: Stop everything — what time is it right now?
The driver pulled the car up by the kerb.

meanings.note: Vocative particle used when addressing someone directly.

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Everyday conversational bridge introducing an inference ('so that means...'), clarification, or gentle pause ('I mean...').

examples.trans: So the house says hello by itself?
Does that mean there is no heating tonight?

meanings.note: Standard noun for day, often used in expressions like 'el-yom' (today).

examples.trans: Today the weather is sunny and warm in Amman.
Have a happy, successful day!
